questions.q: Which combination defines Whipple's triad, the criterion used to decide whether a low glucose is truly pathologic?

A fingerstick below 70 mg/dL on three separate mornings in an asymptomatic patient
A low plasma glucose with a high insulin level and a suppressed C-peptide level

Adrenal or pituitary insufficiency with loss of counter-regulation
Liver failure with depleted hepatic glycogen stores
Sepsis in a critically ill hospitalized patient

Adrenal insufficiency with loss of cortisol counter-regulation
Liver failure with exhausted hepatic glycogen stores
An insulinoma secreting endogenous insulin autonomously
Sulfonylurea ingestion driving endogenous insulin release

questions.q: An alert diabetic inpatient reports tremor and sweating and the bedside fingerstick reads 58 mg/dL. What does the Rule of 15 direct you to do?
